gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at the makers' own US stores on 2026-11-08, ALLPOWERS's $698 P1800 + 400 W kit is priced to the dollar at the P1800 alone ($399) plus the SP037 400 W panel on flash deal ($299), so the bundle saves nothing; that ALLPOWERS's P1800 + 600 W kit is only $100 more ($798); and that BLUETTI's AC180 + 2 × 200 W kit has gone to $1,232, where the AC180 + 200 W kit ($769) plus one $399 SP200L comes to $1,168.
standout_why: I read powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited), voltandvalley.com combo guide and stormwatts.com bundle-vs-separate. Powersized lists only BLUETTI AC180 + 2×200W ($1,232) and Anker C1000 Gen 2 + 400W ($1,349.99 with coupon), says 'Separate price: Not available' for both, and has no ALLPOWERS. Volt & Valley lists Jackery 1000 v2 + 2×200W at $559 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + 2×220W at $919 (Amazon, 2026-11-07), gives no maker-store prices and no ALLPOWERS. StormWatts gives AC180 + 2×200W at $949 (2026-10-16), which no longer matches BLUETTI's store, and has no ALLPOWERS. None of them prices ALLPOWERS's 1 kWh kits against the parts sold separately, or the cheaper route to 400 W of BLUETTI panels.
decides: This confirms ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 as the cheapest 1 kWh + 400 W kit at a maker store ($698), at least $221 under every other maker-priced kit we found. It also changes the advice: the kit carries no discount over the parts, so a shopper can buy them separately for the same money, or pay $100 more for 600 W of panels (the P1800 takes up to 650 W). For BLUETTI, it changes how to buy: skip the $1,232 AC180 + 2×200W kit and take the AC180 + 200W kit plus a second SP200L.
